s1497: Deliberately stopping a vehicle's movement for up to 5 minutes, or longer if this is needed to let passengers in or out or to load or unload the vehicle
s1498: Deliberately stopping a vehicle's movement because of the requirements of traffic control devices or a traffic officer
s1499: Deliberately stopping a vehicle's movement in a stream of traffic
s1501: According to paragraph 11 of Article 5 of the Law of Georgia on Road Traffic, stopping is deliberately stopping a vehicle's movement for up to 5 minutes, or longer if this is needed to let passengers in or out or to load or unload the vehicle. Deliberately stopping a vehicle's movement in a stream of traffic, or because of the requirements of traffic control devices or a traffic officer, is not considered stopping.
s1502: Deliberately stopping a vehicle's movement for more than 5 minutes, when this is not needed to let passengers in or out or to load or unload the vehicle
s1504: According to paragraph 20 of Article 5 of the Law of Georgia on Road Traffic, parking is deliberately stopping a vehicle's movement for more than 5 minutes, when this is not needed to let passengers in or out or to load or unload the vehicle.

s1518: In this situation, is the driver prohibited from stopping the car at the place shown by the arrow?
s1519: According to paragraph 3.27 of Chapter 3 (Prohibitory signs) of Annex 1 to the Law of Georgia on Road Traffic, road sign 3.27 "No stopping" prohibits vehicles from both stopping and parking. According to subparagraph "e" of the Note to the same Chapter, signs 3.26–3.30 apply after the sign, from the place where it is installed to the nearest intersection, and in a built-up area with no intersection, to the end of the built-up area. s1635: Which of these identification signs is the "distinguishing sign of the state of registration" for a vehicle registered in Georgia and travelling internationally?
s1636: According to subparagraph "c" of paragraph 2 of Article 19 of the Law of Georgia on Road Traffic, the "distinguishing sign of the state of registration" is the distinguishing sign of a vehicle registered in Georgia and travelling internationally. The sign is elliptical, with axes at least 0.175 m X 0.115 m long. It bears Georgia's international code "GE". The Latin letters must be at least 0.08 m high, drawn with strokes at least 0.01 m wide. The letters are painted in black on a white background (the white background may be made of reflective material). The sign must be fixed to the vehicle so that it cannot be mistaken for the registration number (state number plate) and does not make it harder to read.
s1637: Which of these identification signs is the "warning triangle"?
s1638: According to paragraph 5 of Article 52 of the Law of Georgia on Road Traffic, the "warning triangle" is an equilateral triangular plate with sides at least 0.4 metres long and a red border at least 0.05 metres wide. The middle of the triangle may be hollow or painted in a light colour. The red border must not let light through or must have a reflective strip. The plate must be designed so that it can stand steadily in an upright position.
